en.name: Lucius III
en.summary: A pope who, working with Frederick Barbarossa, issued the decree Ad abolendam, an early formal framework for prosecuting heresy.
en.body: Lucius III, like several predecessors, found Rome largely inhospitable to papal residence and governed mostly from northern Italian cities. In 1184, meeting with Frederick Barbarossa at Verona, he issued the decree Ad abolendam, establishing cooperative procedures between church and secular authorities for identifying and punishing heresy — a foundational document in the later development of inquisitorial procedure.
